clue.text: Film set in a prison yard attentive to detail

indicators.note: something set in a place is placed inside it, so the film goes within the other letters

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'per annum' or 'ten pounds a head'
the nick is British slang for a prison
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A film crew shooting in a prison yard is praised for its careful eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film set' reads as a studio set, but set is the insertion signal. 'a' meaning per, as in fifty pence a go, is a common trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernickety means fussy, overly concerned with small particulars, a British informal word.

clue.text: Top-class potassium compound? No thanks

indicators.note: 'no' tells the solver to do without the word that follows it

blocks.note: potash is a potassium compound, potassium carbonate
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A chemist offered a fancy potassium compound declines politely.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TA out of POTASH. Ta is everyday British for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal for upper-class or smart and expensive.

clue.text: Tree, something harder than 12 Bellamy regularly chopped

indicators.note: chopped at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the name survives

blocks.note: the answer to 12 is a soft pop genre; rock is the harder music
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: David Bellamy, the TV botanist, takes an axe to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellamy suggests the botanist David Bellamy, but here it is just letters; 12 is the cross-reference to EASY LISTENING.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock elm is a North American species of elm tree with very hard wood.

clue.text: Is dictionary wrong about describing personal traits?

indicators.note: spelt wrong, these letters come out in a muddled order
the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a dictionary errs in its definitions of character traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does double duty here: it is both C and the signal that C sits inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiosyncratic means peculiar to an individual, characterising one person's habits.

clue.text: Important part of brick ingle arrangement

indicators.note: read with 'part', it says the answer is a portion taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the end of brick across ingle into arrangement

explanation.surface: A builder describes the key element of a brick fireplace layout; an ingle is a hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The part is a theatrical role: Shakespeare's title character, one of the great parts for an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is a major Shakespearean role, so an important acting part.

clue.text: Baths adult breaking wind

definitions.note: wind as a collective noun for wind instruments, standing for a plural

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the letter lands within the other word

blocks.note: A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up in the bath breaks wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The schoolboy surface hides that 'wind' means brass and woodwind players' instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubas are large brass instruments, belonging to an orchestra's wind section.

clue.text: Inspection that is probing German carmaker

indicators.note: something probing goes into another thing, so the first letters sit inside the second

blocks.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An inspection is investigating Volkswagen.
explanation.definitionFit: A view can mean a look at or examination of something, as in a private viewing.

clue.text: Hint as expressed by Federation enemy just not on!

indicators.note: the phrase literally asks for the two-letter word 'on' to be absent

blocks.note: said in a language, as in 'expressed in French'
the Klingons are foes of the Federation in Star Trek

explanation.surface: A clue put in Klingon is just not on, a Trekkie protests.
explanation.walkthrough: IN KLINGON, with ON dropped from the end, gives IN KLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suggestion or faint notion of something.

clue.text: Red and white specialist wide player full of energy crossing 22

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside
crossing is taken as having a word put across the middle, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a winger plays out wide in football or rugby
E is the symbol for energy
the answer to 22 is NOISE, and a row is a noise

explanation.surface: A football winger in red and white strip, bursting with energy, crosses the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Red and white looks like a football kit, but it means wines.
explanation.definitionFit: A winegrower cultivates vines to make wine, both red and white varieties.

clue.text: Very smart clubs quitting Russian resort

indicators.note: something that quits leaves, so its letter is taken away

blocks.note: C is the card suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Fashionable nightclubs are closing down in a Russian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final C of SO CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sochi is a Black Sea resort city in Russia that hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics.

clue.text: A US citizen, New England skipper cycles round to welcome supporters

indicators.note: letters cycled round move from one end of the name to the other
to welcome guests is to take them in, so the following word goes inside

blocks.note: Harry Kane captains the England football team

explanation.surface: An American from New England, a boat skipper, goes cycling with fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New England' looks like one unit, but New stands alone and England qualifies the skipper, who is the national football captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nebraskan is a native or resident of Nebraska, a state of the USA.

clue.text: US ban enraged minced European imported beef supplier

indicators.note: imported goods are brought in, so this letter goes into the mix
minced meat is chopped up, so these letters are cut up and reassembled

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An American ban on imported minced meat angers a European beef producer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of cattle raised for its beef.

clue.text: Pop gets insanely irritated, interrupted by yours truly

indicators.note: letters interrupted by something have it put in their midst
irritated letters are agitated and stirred up out of order

explanation.surface: Dad gets insanely irritated when the narrator interrupts him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a father in the surface, but it is pop music; 'insanely' also hints at the anagram while being part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy listening is a genre of light popular music, soft and melodic.

clue.text: Boycott's old yarn mentioned archetypical village XI fast bowler

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so it is the sound of the word that counts

blocks.note: to black something is to boycott it, so 'Boycott's' is 'black is'
a myth is an ancient tale

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire cricketer, tells an old story about a village team's fast bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott suggests the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott, but means to black. BLACKS MYTH said aloud is the answer. A village cricket XI's fearsome quick bowler is traditionally the brawny village smith.
explanation.definitionFit: The blacksmith, a strong forge-worker, is the stock character who bowls fast for a village cricket eleven.

clue.text: Sole newspaper in France pruned Advisory Board

indicators.note: a pruned plant has its end cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Le Monde is a French daily paper

explanation.surface: The only French newspaper to cut its advisory board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' reads as 'only' but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon sole is a European flatfish, so a type of sole; dab is another flatfish.

clue.text: Slowly, madam undressed Joe DiMaggio at last

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so the word loses its outside letters
at last points to the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe slowly undresses for her husband, the baseball star Joe DiMaggio.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe DiMaggio reads as one name but splits: Joe is GI, and DiMaggio supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical direction meaning play at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Dark gold upturned hat

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned upside down reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A dark hat with gold, turned up at the brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' sounds like a hat brim, but it flips the gold symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Warms toast

blocks.note: first meaning: gladdens or heartens someone
second meaning: the word said when glasses are raised

explanation.walkthrough: 'Warms toast' sounds like reheating bread; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort or warm them, and 'Cheers!' is the drinking salutation.

clue.text: Disclosed electronic car, limited edition

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An electric car is revealed in a limited edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited edition' looks like a phrase, but limited belongs to the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolve once meant to unfold or open out, so evolved can mean revealed or unrolled.

clue.text: Lazy Joe Biden leaving Jack furiously holding line

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed
done furiously, the letters are thrown into wild disorder
holding something means keeping it inside

explanation.surface: Joe Biden, lazy, leaves while the Union Jack angrily keeps the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove J from JOE BIDEN, rearrange the rest, and put L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone idle is a British idiom for extremely lazy.

clue.text: Daughter, 26, about to take on a Republican ultraconservative

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A daughter is about to take on a Republican hardliner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' is the anagram signal and 'to take on' the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard is someone stubbornly resistant to change, a reactionary.

clue.text: Estate reported ceasefire

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the clue gives a sound rather than a spelling

blocks.note: a ceasefire is a pause in the firing

explanation.surface: A country estate reports a halt to the shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' looks like land for a shoot, but it is an estate car.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting brake is an old British name for an estate car or station wagon.

clue.text: Wound up student binned report

indicators.note: something binned is thrown away, so that letter is dropped
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A tense student throws a school report in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' looks like agitated, but wound is the noun and up the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be a loud bang, such as a gun's, which is a noise.

clue.text: Mock buffoon losing his way

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so these letters are taken out

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: People mock a clown who has got lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to scoff at or deride someone.

clue.text: Sarcastic, resourceful opener for Notts dismissed for century

definitions.note: invective is usually a noun; as an adjective it means abusive

indicators.note: one batter dismissed for another means one letter leaves and another takes its place

blocks.note: the first letter of Notts, Nottinghamshire county cricket club

explanation.surface: A sarcastic commentator on a Nottinghamshire opening batsman out for a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener and century suggest cricket; they are just the letter N and the numeral C.
explanation.definitionFit: Invective, as an adjective, describes abusive, bitterly denunciatory language.

clue.text: Clearing backlog, lad erases files

indicators.note: files is read as stores away, so the words keep the answer tucked within them

blocks.note: spans the end of backlog, all of lad, and the start of erases

explanation.surface: An office junior clears a backlog by deleting files.
explanation.walkthrough: Clearing reads as tidying the backlog, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is an open space in a forest, a clearing among trees.

clue.text: Stash heroin and ecstasy I had acquired

indicators.note: letters acquired are taken in, so they end up held between the others

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A drug user confesses to stashing heroin and ecstasy they had obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to stash it away out of sight.

clue.text: Note opposition benches, beginning to reflect, think again

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
con as in pros and cons: against
the benches in Parliament are where each side sits

explanation.surface: An MP notes that the opposition benches are starting to reflect and rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposition benches' reads as one Westminster phrase, but the two words clue separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to review a decision and possibly change it.
